verdict.rationale: Homebrew's core value proposition is a large, actively maintained formula/cask registry, taps for extending it, and independent evidence (comm-18) confirms broad package availability and fast version updates versus alternatives like MacPorts; docs also show bundler support for many ecosystems (npm, cargo, Go, etc.) broadening what can be installed. Some community friction exists around packaging difficulty and stale taps (homebrew-comm-6, homebrew-comm-7) but these are edge-case caveats, not evidence the registry itself fails to deliver broad package availability. Missing for 10: independent quantitative data on total package count/registry size and update cadence beyond anecdote.
